summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Key evolutionary links: Echinoderms link deuterostome ancestry via bilateral larvae (bipinnaria/pluteus); Hemichordates have a stomochord (NOT a notochord) and excrete via the proboscis gland.

conceptBreakdown.content: These enterocoelous deuterostome invertebrates represent the immediate sister groups to Phylum Chordata.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Phylum Echinodermata (Spiny-Skinned Animals)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Phylum Echinodermata (Spiny-Skinned Animals)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ECHINODERM SYMMETRY METAMORPHOSIS
                      
  Bilaterally Symmetrical Larva ──[Metamorphosis]──► Pentamerous Radially Symmetrical Adult
  (e.g., Bipinnaria / Pluteus)                       (e.g., Starfish / Sea Urchin)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Symmetry Metamorphosis**: Exclusively marine; free-swimming larvae are **bilaterally symmetrical**, while sessile/benthic adults exhibit **pentamerous radial symmetry**.
• **Water Vascular System (Ambulacral System)**: Enterocoelic coelomic hydraulic pipeline used for locomotion, food capture, gas exchange, and excretion.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Water Vascular Pathway & Special Physiology
conceptBreakdown.title: Water Vascular Pathway & Special Physiology
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
WATER VASCULAR SYSTEM PATHWAY
                       
   Madreporite ──► Stone Canal ──► Ring Canal ──► Radial Canals ──► Tube Feet (Podia)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Excretory System**: **COMPLETELY ABSENT**. Nitrogenous waste (ammonia) diffuses directly across tube feet and dermal branchiae (papulae).
• **Endoskeleton & Pincers**: Mesodermal calcareous ossicles and jaw-like surface pincers (**Pedicellariae**) for cleaning.
• **Key Taxa**: *Asterias* (starfish), *Echinus* (sea urchin), *Antedon* (sea lily), *Cucumaria* (sea cucumber), *Ophiura* (brittle star).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Phylum Hemichordata (Acorn Worms)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Phylum Hemichordata (Acorn Worms)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **The Stomochord**: Anterior buccal diverticulum (*Stomochord*) extending into the proboscis; structurally and embryologically **distinct from a true notochord**.
• **Body Triad & Excretion**: Worm-like marine body divided into anterior **Proboscis**, intermediate **Collar**, and long **Trunk**. Excretion occurs via a single glomerulus called the **Proboscis Gland**.
• **Respiration & Larva**: Pharyngeal gill slits; indirect development via ciliated **Tornaria Larva** (morphologically similar to echinoderm bipinnaria larvae).
• **Key Taxa**: *Balanoglossus*, *Saccoglossus*.
